input.question: Do the effects of nicotine increase like alcohol?
input.ground_truth: Quite the opposite. 1st cig of the day you mightttt get a buzz. After that they don't do anything but soothe the addiction. Booze on the other hand will add on to your drunkenness. Only thing smoking a bunch of cigs in succession will do is make your throat feel like a rusty tomato in the morning.

Question: Do the effects of nicotine increase like alcohol?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a toy car and you can make it go faster by pressing a button. If you press the button a little, the car goes a little faster. If you press it more, it goes even faster.

Nicotine is like that button. If you have a little bit of nicotine, it does a little bit to your body. If you have more nicotine, it does more.

Alcohol is a bit like a different toy. If you drink a little juice, you don’t feel much different. But if you drink more juice (but let’s say it’s special juice that can make you wobbly), you start to feel wobbly and silly. If you drink even more, you feel much more wobbly.

So, both nicotine and alcohol can do more things to your body if you have more of them. But they are different kinds of “buttons” and make your body feel different ways.

But grown-ups say both are not good for you, especially if you have a lot.
